To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) skin diseases are common and cause significant morbidity; 2) most of these diseases are preventable, treatable, or both; 3) the community is not aware that these diseases are preventably or treatably; 4) the community is poorly educated on skin disease; 5) people with skin disease are poorly educated; 6) people with skin diseases are poorly informed; 7) people with skin disorders are not seeking the advice of a medical practitioner;

the prevalence of skin disease in the Australian community is high, that most of the disease is managed by the community, that the quality of management is substandard, and that the quality of care can be improved with education of the community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epidemiology of skin disease in the Australian community, the impact of skin disease in terms of quality of life, and the effectiveness of treatment.
the epidemiology of common skin diseases in the community, with the aim of improving the health and well being of all Australians.
the epidemiology and public health of skin disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the public is not well served by the present system of skin health in Australia.
there is a lack of awareness of the need for early diagnosis and treatment of skin cancer, and that this is the most important public health problem in dermatology today.
we are in the middle of a skin cancer epidemic.
